name: Hadean

facts.sky: a huge, close Moon filling much of the sky, streaked by meteors
facts.air: no free oxygen, only carbon dioxide, nitrogen, water vapour and volcanic gas
facts.climate: infernal, cooling from a global magma ocean
facts.sea: the first oceans just condensing onto black basalt, boiling near vents
facts.land: young, unstable crust, endless volcanism and lava plains
facts.life: none, at most the first prebiotic chemistry in hot pools

seed: You stand on black basalt still warm underfoot, and the Moon hangs enormous and near, close enough to fill a third of the sky. There is no life, no oxygen, only steam, the reek of sulphur, and an ocean just beginning to condense out of a scalding sky.

name: Archean

facts.sky: an orange, methane-hazy sky under a Sun that burns noticeably fainter
facts.air: no oxygen, rich in methane, carbon dioxide and nitrogen
facts.climate: warm oceans despite the dim young Sun
facts.sea: green, iron-rich seas covering nearly the whole planet
facts.land: small grey continents beginning to assemble, volcanic islands
facts.life: single-celled microbes and stromatolites, layered mounds built by microbial mats; cyanobacteria appear late

seed: An orange methane haze softens a Sun that burns fainter than you know it. Green iron-rich seas stretch to every horizon, broken only by low volcanic islands and slick domes of microbial rock, the stromatolites, the only architecture on Earth.

name: Paleoproterozoic

facts.air: oxygen appearing for the first time in the Great Oxidation Event, poisoning the old anaerobic world
facts.climate: the Huronian glaciation, one of the earliest global ice ages
facts.sea: oceans rusting, laying down banded iron formations in red and grey
facts.life: microbes, and the first eukaryotic cells with a nucleus

seed: The air itself is changing: cyanobacteria have begun exhaling oxygen, and it is rusting the oceans, laying down iron in banded red and grey. Somewhere in this poisoning of the old anaerobic world, the first cells with a nucleus are quietly assembling.

name: Mesoproterozoic

facts.climate: unusually stable and warm, the so-called boring billion
facts.sea: green to purple microbial oceans, sulphurous in places
facts.land: the supercontinents Columbia and then Rodinia, barren red rock
facts.life: eukaryotes diversifying, the first sexual reproduction, microbial mats everywhere, no animals

seed: Nothing much happens here, and that is the wonder of it, a billion years of warm, stable, sulphurous seas. Microbial mats carpet the shallows, the supercontinent broods under a pale sky, and no animal has ever moved.

name: Neoproterozoic

facts.air: oxygen rising toward levels that can support animals
facts.climate: the Cryogenian Snowball Earth, ice reaching the equator, then a thaw
facts.sea: under ice, then teeming Ediacaran seafloors
facts.life: the first large multicellular life, the soft Ediacaran fauna of fronds, discs and quilted forms

seed: The whole planet has been ice, white to the equator, and now it thaws into strange gardens. On the seafloor the Ediacarans wave: fronds and quilted discs and ribbed forms, the first large life, soft and mouthless and utterly unlike anything that will follow.

name: Cambrian

facts.sea: the Cambrian Explosion: trilobites, the metre-long predator Anomalocaris, and the first animals with eyes, shells and limbs
facts.land: still bare rock, no life above the tideline

seed: The shallow sea seethes with invention. Trilobites plough the mud, the metre-long Anomalocaris sweeps the water with its grasping arms, and eyes, brand new in the world, are everywhere. The land above the tideline is still bare stone.

name: Ordovician

facts.climate: warm, ending in a sudden severe ice age
facts.sea: vast shallow seas, straight-shelled nautiloids, and the first coral reefs
facts.land: only a green film of the earliest mosses and liverworts, hugging wet ground
facts.life: an explosion of marine diversity, then the end-Ordovician mass extinction

seed: Over reefs built by the first corals, straight-shelled nautiloids hunt in warm shallow seas. On the naked land, only a green film of the earliest mosses and liverworts has gained a foothold, hugging the wet edges of the world.

name: Silurian

facts.sea: jawed fish and giant sea scorpions, the eurypterids, over reefs
facts.land: the first vascular plants, low leafless green stems, with the first millipedes and arachnids
facts.life: life gaining a real foothold on land for the first time

seed: The first real gardens climb the shore: low forests of leafless green stems, the first vascular plants, with millipedes and early arachnids threading between them. In the sea, jawed fish and giant sea scorpions have begun to rule.

name: Devonian

facts.sea: the Age of Fishes, thick with armoured giants and the first sharks
facts.land: the first true forests, and the first four-limbed tetrapods hauling out of the water
facts.life: vertebrates making the move onto land, ending in the Late Devonian extinctions

seed: This is the Age of Fishes, the seas thick with armoured giants and the first sharks. On land the first true forests rise, and in a muddy shallow something with four limbs and lungs is hauling itself, for the first time, out of the water.

name: Carboniferous

facts.air: oxygen near its all-time peak, fuelling giant insects
facts.land: immense coal-forming swamp forests of tree-ferns and clubmosses, dragonflies the size of hawks, millipedes longer than a person
facts.life: the first reptiles and the amniote egg appear

seed: You breathe air richer in oxygen than any human ever will, and the swamp answers with giants: dragonflies the size of hawks, millipedes longer than you are tall. Endless coal forests of tree-ferns and clubmosses drip in the heat.

name: Permian

facts.climate: hot and dry across a vast continental interior
facts.land: the supercontinent Pangaea, red deserts running for thousands of miles, sail-backed synapsids that are distant mammal ancestors
facts.life: ending in the Great Dying, Earth's largest mass extinction

seed: Pangaea, one vast continent, bakes under a hard sun, its red interior a desert that runs for thousands of miles. Sail-backed synapsids, the distant ancestors of mammals, move through the dry margins, unaware that the greatest dying in Earth's history is coming.

name: Triassic

facts.climate: hot and dry on a recovering, single supercontinent
facts.land: the first dinosaurs and the first small mammals, both newly appeared
facts.life: a world rebuilding after near-total death

seed: The world is recovering from near-total death, hot and dry across a single supercontinent. Among the survivors, two quiet newcomers have appeared, the first small dinosaurs and the first tiny mammals, both waiting for a world to inherit.

name: Jurassic

facts.air: warm, high carbon dioxide, no polar ice
facts.climate: lush and green to the poles
facts.sea: plesiosaurs and ichthyosaurs, high sea levels
facts.land: giant sauropods and Allosaurus among tree-ferns and cycads, and the very first birds

seed: Warm, wet, and green to the poles, the land shudders under sauropods the length of ships. Allosaurus hunts beneath tree-ferns and cycads, and overhead, on leathery feathered wings, the very first birds cross a sky without ice at either end of the world.

name: Cretaceous

facts.sea: mosasaurs and ammonites in warm shallow seas
facts.land: Tyrannosaurus and Triceratops, and the first flowering plants and bees spreading scent across the world
facts.life: ending abruptly with the Chicxulub asteroid impact and the extinction of the non-bird dinosaurs

seed: Flowers exist now, and bees, scenting a world that has never smelled of blossom before. Tyrannosaurus moves through it, and Triceratops, and out beyond the warm inland seas nothing yet suggests the asteroid already falling toward the future.

name: Paleogene

facts.climate: a hothouse world with a sharp warm spike, cooling later
facts.sea: the first whales returning to the sea
facts.land: mammals radiating into the empty world, giant flightless birds, and the first primates in the branches
facts.life: life reorganising after the death of the dinosaurs

seed: The dinosaurs are gone, and into the silence the mammals pour: small at first, then bold, filling forests and plains and, astonishingly, returning to the sea as the first whales. Among the branches, something small and big-eyed, an early primate, watches.

name: Neogene

facts.land: grasslands spreading across the world, grazing herds, apes, and the first upright-walking hominins in the African woodlands
facts.life: the stage being set for humanity

seed: Grass has conquered the world, and with it come the grazers and the herds. In the drying African woodlands an ape has come down from the trees and begun, on two legs, to walk out across the open ground toward everything that comes next.

name: Pleistocene

facts.climate: repeated ice ages, ice sheets advancing and retreating
facts.land: mammoths, woolly rhinos and sabre-toothed cats across cold tundra
facts.life: Neanderthals, and then Homo sapiens, watching the herds from the edge of the ice

seed: Ice sheets grind south and pull back and grind south again. Mammoths and woolly rhinos breathe steam across the tundra, sabre-tooths shadow the herds, and by firelight at the edge of the ice, people, both Neanderthal and newly arrived Homo sapiens, watch the dark.

name: Holocene

facts.climate: a brief, unusually stable warm interglacial
facts.land: the first fields and cities, every language, war and song, the whole of recorded history
facts.life: humanity everywhere, the age you were born into

seed: The ice has loosened its grip, and in this brief, unusual warmth everything you call history happens at once: the first fields, the first cities, every language and war and song. It is a thin, calm sliver of time, and you have always lived inside it.
